items.summary: The brand's 38 physical stores and online site will continue to operate while receivers review its operations.

items.title: Jungle Ventures targets two IPOs a year from its portfolio
items.summary: The early-stage VC firm is preparing startups such as Moglix and Livspace for public markets while closing in on a fifth fund that will push its India bets past $1 billion.

items.title: Snack makers tweak trade margins, engineer pouches to break ₹5 pack habit
items.summary: Rising costs of potatoes, edible oil and packaging are squeezing margins on entry-level packs, prompting snack makers to push larger SKUs, rethink packaging and expand premium offerings.

items.title: From tunnel boring machines to rockets and pod taxis, L&T explores new manufacturing bets
items.summary: Larsen and Toubro is exploring at least half a dozen new businesses ranging from nuclear fuel rods and tunnel boring machines to rockets and drones and their components

items.title: Inside India newsletter: India weighs a tax cut to win over foreign investors. Will it work?
items.summary: Foreign investors are losing their appetite for Indian equities, with their holdings touching an all-time low of 14%.

items.title: Copper is booming but not everyone is striking gold
items.summary: As selling prices soar, the red metal frenzy favours miners over smelters

items.title: China’s critical minerals dominance leaves UK ‘dangerously exposed’, MPs warn
items.summary: Committee chair Liam Byrne says failure to diversify supplies continues to pose significant risks to Britain’s future security

items.title: Big FMCG companies outgrow market as smaller rivals get squeezed by costs and slowing rural demand
items.summary: India's fast-moving consumer goods sector has experienced a slowdown in volume growth amid rising costs. Rural demand has weakened, impacting smaller regional manufacturers while larger companies thrive. Hindustan Unilever, Marico, and other major firms reported robust growth figures. Smaller players are particularly vulnerable due to their limited capacity to manage current challenges.

items.title: A 'demand decade' ahead for energy? BP, Baker Hughes CEOs weigh the investment outlook
items.summary: Rising energy demand offers investment opportunities, but geopolitical risks and oil price uncertainty cloud the outlook, executives and an analyst said.

items.title: What was really behind Wednesday's monster rally? Trump quickly making peace
items.summary: The stock market skyrocketed after a decisive sweep for Democrats in the 2026 midterm elections, a move that Trump's reaction added to.

items.title: Elon Musk's millions failed to deliver Republican wins in fierce midterms
items.summary: Musk spent nearly $500m in the 2026 US midterm elections, an individual election spending record.

items.title: FitLab Blames Bankruptcy on Loss of Nike Partnership, Trump Tariffs
items.summary: FitLab Inc., which makes cardio equipment and runs boutique fitness studios, said it filed bankruptcy following disruptions to its supply chain and the loss of a key deal with Nike Inc.

items.title: India proposes 1% mandatory blending of green jet fuel from January
items.summary: India has introduced a draft policy for the mandatory blending of sustainable aviation fuel for international flights. The initial blending requirement is set at 1%, increasing to 5% by 2030, and 20% by 2040. Airlines must source approximately 90% of their aviation turbine fuel from international airports to curb economic tankering. Non-compliance may lead to penalties for airlines and oil marketing companies in this proposal.

items.title: Govt plans instant ban on manufacturing of drugs failing key quality tests
items.summary: Pharma companies could have their drug licenses suspended immediately if quality tests indicate failure. The health ministry's proposed changes aim to protect public health by enforcing swift action on substandard medications. Regulators would take action upon receiving a government analyst's report declaring a drug not of standard quality. Manufacturers would need to perform a root cause analysis and implement corrective actions to lift the suspension.

items.title: Kellogg's admits snap, crackle and pop is quieter after uproar over Rice Krispies recipe change
items.summary: The cereal giant has changed the recipes for Rice Krispies and Coco Pops, sparking a backlash online.

items.title: MIAL seeks to shift 14 international flights to Navi Mumbai Airport by Nov 3
items.summary: Mumbai International Airport has proposed shifting flights to 14 international destinations to the new Navi Mumbai International Airport. This move aims to free up capacity for the redevelopment of Terminal 1 at the current airport. If airlines do not voluntarily surrender slots, the airport operator plans to execute the transition. Passengers flying to Gulf and Asian destinations may have to use the new airport instead.

items.title: Mercedes plans bigger India play with greater localisation of parts
items.summary: Mercedes-Benz plans to increase its local manufacturing efforts while expanding its supplier base in India. The luxury carmaker expects to achieve record annual sales if the current trend continues. Ola Kallenius, the global chairman, highlighted the potential for Indian suppliers to support global operations. The company has committed an additional investment of ₹200 crore, raising total investments to ₹3,200 crore.

items.title: Big factories dominate India's manufacturing output, Annual Survey of Industries shows
items.summary: India's manufacturing sector is characterised by a significant concentration in large factories generating substantial output. Factories producing over ₹500 crore contribute to more than three-fifths of total value added. Smaller factories represent a large number but have minimal output and value contribution.

items.title: Battery component makers may get up to 50% capital subsidy
items.summary: The ministry of heavy industries is evaluating various subsidy models to enhance domestic battery component manufacturing capacity. Proposed support includes capital subsidies and sales-linked incentives to promote local production. India aims for sufficient manufacturing capacity to support 50 GWh of annual battery cell production by 2032. Current costs of battery materials are significantly higher compared to those from China.

items.title: Cabinet approves VGF plan for grid-scale energy storage with Rs 14,500 crore support
items.summary: The Union Cabinet has approved a significant ₹14,500 crore funding scheme to develop 92 GWh of energy storage capacity. This initiative supports both hydro pumped storage and battery energy storage systems aimed at accelerating renewable energy. Additionally, a scheme has been approved for processing critical minerals like lithium and nickel to reduce import dependency. The government aims to modernize its statistical system with a ₹4,371.10 crore scheme.

items.title: Sebi eases KYC norms for NRIs, OCIs and foreign nationals, allows digital onboarding from overseas
items.summary: Securities and Exchange Board of India has relaxed Know Your Client requirements for overseas investors. This change enables non-resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India, and foreign nationals to onboard digitally. Individuals from FATF-compliant countries can now submit KYC details remotely without being in India. Intermediaries are allowed to rely on existing KYC records and conduct video verifications when necessary.

items.title: Trump diesel deal with Russia falters as US fuel supplies hit 20-year low
items.summary: Two tankers change course in setback to White House gambit to lower fuel prices and shore up political support

items.title: New orders & robust demand lift India's October services growth to 4-month high
items.summary: Growth in India's services sector increased to a four-month high in October due to strong domestic demand and business orders. The HSBC Services Business Activity Index rose to 55.8, reflecting improved business conditions. Conversely, manufacturing activity showed a slight decline, easing to a PMI of 54.7. While input prices continued to rise, the rate of increase was the slowest in over six years.

items.title: US slaps sanctions on Indian, Turkish firms and people for aiding Iran
items.summary: The sanctions are part of the Trump administration's "Operation Economic Outcast," which aims to cut off Iran's ability to sell oil to fund the war with the US and Israel. Treasury unveiled the new sanctions a day after Democrats made huge gains in midterm elections, winning control of both houses of Congress as voters expressed anger about the Iran war and its impact in fueling US inflation.

items.title: Trump's midterm setback may give India an edge in trade deal
items.summary: US has sought to allay concerns that the Republicans’ midterm election defeat could derail trade talks with India, with an American embassy spokesperson saying that President Donald Trump remains firmly in charge of Washington’s trade agenda

items.title: Explained: Why could a weak monsoon derail India's ambitious ethanol blending programme?
items.summary: India’s weak monsoon and rising food prices are putting food security ahead of ethanol production, potentially pushing the country’s fuel-blending rate below its 20% target and increasing reliance on imported crude.

items.title: Over half of street vendors may cut UPI acceptance if 0.4% MDR is introduced: ISB study
items.summary: More than 67% of street vendors in India currently accept UPI payments for transactions. A proposed 0.4% merchant discount rate could lead to reduced acceptance among vendors. Concerns arise particularly for vendor-supplier transactions, as many vendors make payments above ₹2,000. A significant portion of vendors faced additional charges from suppliers and might pass costs onto customers.

items.title: TRAI's new Network Anubhav platform to map real-world network speeds, call quality
items.summary: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India recently introduced the Network Anubhav Platform for consumers. This new platform allows users to compare mobile and broadband networks based on location and performance. Consumers can view network tests, filter results, and make informed choices about service providers.

items.title: Sirolimus-coated balloon shows 8-percentage-point advantage in three-year peripheral artery trial
items.summary: Patients treated with sirolimus-coated balloons were more likely to remain free from repeat procedures to reopen blocked leg arteries than those receiving paclitaxel-coated balloons, according to three-year results from the SIRONA clinical trial presented at TCT 2026. While both treatments showed similar improvements in walking ability and quality of life, researchers said the findings require confirmation through five-year follow-up.

items.title: US to loan about a third of heating oil reserve in bid to tame prices
items.summary: The US Energy Department will loan 300,000 barrels of fuel oil from its emergency heating reserve to four companies to ease supply pressures and rising prices ahead of winter. The release, nearly a third of the reserve, follows calls from bipartisan senators as Middle East disruptions linked to the Iran war push fuel costs higher.

items.title: Government prepares draft sustainable aviation fuels policy; moots mandatory blending in ATF from 2027
items.summary: The civil aviation ministry has circulated the draft National Policy on Sustainable Aviation Fuels which mandates use of only indigenously manufactured SAF to be blended with Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF).

items.title: LTCG tax relief on cards? FM acknowledges FPI concerns as SEBI, FICCI push for reforms in Budget 2027
items.summary: FM Nirmala Sitharaman said the government recognizes investor concerns about India’s investment climate and will consider feedback as it seeks to sustain growth near 7%. She acknowledged rising foreign investment outflows.

items.title: International airlines have choice to shift to Navi Mumbai airport or suspend operations temporarily: Adani Airports CEO
items.summary: International airlines currently operating from Mumbai airport are given options to temporarily suspend operations or relocate. Discussions are ongoing with various international carriers regarding this transition. Indian airlines such as IndiGo and Air India have agreed to shift certain operations.

items.title: HDFC Bank to offer deposits under Capital Gains Accounts Scheme
items.summary: HDFC Bank has received government authorisation to offer deposits under the Capital Gains Accounts Scheme (CGAS), 1988. The facility will allow taxpayers to park unused capital gains in savings accounts or fixed deposits for up to three years while retaining eligibility for applicable tax exemptions and earning interest on their deposits.

items.title: Piyush Goyal sets March 2027 deadline for digitisation of DGFT services, aims to end physical visits
items.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal has set March 31, 2027, as the deadline for complete digitisation of DGFT services, including licence, permit and SCOMET approvals. From April 1, businesses will no longer need physical visits to government offices for these services. The move also includes digitising historical records and simplifying procedures.

items.title: Nitin Gadkari flags Indian highways, expressways still lack perfect signage
items.summary: Nitin Gadkari highlighted the need for better project preparation and accountability in urban road development initiatives. He expressed concern over the lack of proper signage on Indian highways and its role in accidents. Gadkari mentioned nearly 5 lakh road accidents each year, causing 1.8 lakh deaths in India. He proposed that urban planning requires integrated approaches among various transport agencies to optimize public resources.

items.title: Blood banks targeted in latest European fridge cyberattacks
items.summary: French blood banks were hit by cybersecurity attacks on Monday, with hackers cranking up temperatures in refrigerators storing blood.

items.title: Blue wave sweeps markets back towards normality
items.summary: US midterm results may point to more restraints on the Trump administration

items.title: China steps up defence of stock market in bid to revive AI boom
items.summary: ETFs commonly used by Beijing to support market see second-highest net inflows on record

items.title: Solvay strikes rare earths deal that will reduce global dependence on China
items.summary: Supply from Brazilian mine will bolster high-tech magnet production in Europe and US

items.title: U.S. midterm elections in pictures: Democrats' sweeping victories deliver rebuke to Trump
items.summary: Democrats scored sweeping victories in the U.S. midterm elections on Wednesday, flipping key Republican-held seats in Congress.

items.title: India sees some trade relief, new risks after US midterm vote
items.summary: A bruised Trump after US midterm election results gives New Delhi some breathing room in negotiations over an India-US trade deal, reducing pressure to agree to terms it sees as unfavourable.

items.title: US midterm election results 2026: India sees some trade relief, new risks after US midterm vote
items.summary: Indian officials are cautiously optimistic about the recent US midterm election results and their implications. While the election reduces trade tension, it introduces new uncertainties for US-India relations. Analysts suggest it is too early to gauge the long-term effects of these political changes. The potential for increased tariffs still looms due to ongoing investigations.

items.title: Services sector growth hits a four-month peak in October, PMI survey shows
items.summary: Driven by strong domestic demand, HSBC's India Services PMI rose to 55.8 in October as cost pressures eased to a six-year low, even as export orders and hiring slowed.

items.title: India-EU FTA to simplify and reinforce corporate cooperation, says Swedish Ambassador Petra Menander
items.summary: The proposed India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) will simplify and reinforce bilateral corporate collaboration, said Sweden's Ambassador to India Petra Menander, pointing to expanded opportunities for technology transfers and joint industrial initiatives.

items.title: Trump's midterm setback may put India under pressure for quick trade deal on US terms: GTRI
items.summary: Amid electoral challenges, US President Donald Trump is likely to ramp up pressure on India to seal a trade deal. This potential agreement would require India to decrease import tariffs on US goods while the US keeps its tariffs intact. Analysts caution that such an arrangement may breach WTO MFN principles, undermining India's trade credibility. Additionally, compromising energy security and development aspirations could have serious implications.

items.title: RBI sets up panel with banks, market players to review financial market issues
items.summary: India's central bank has formed a technical consultative committee to engage with market participants on financial issues. This committee will include seven external members from various financial institutions and will address market infrastructure. It will examine the functioning and efficiency of money and related derivative markets. Members will assess both domestic and international developments that impact these markets.

items.title: India's services growth accelerates to 55.8 in October, cost pressures ease to six-year low
items.summary: India's services sector activity expanded at its fastest pace in four months in October, with the HSBC India Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rising to 55.8 from 55.2 in September, while input cost inflation eased to its lowest level in more than six years, according to data released by S&P Global on Wednesday.

items.title: Piyush Goyal holds talks with Danish minister to expand economic partnership
items.summary: India and Denmark are actively exploring various opportunities to strengthen their economic engagement and partnerships. The discussions between Piyush Goyal and Martin Lidegaard emphasized collaborative efforts in trade, investment, and industrial cooperation. Approximately 250 Danish companies operate in India, employing over 100,000 individuals while showing strong interest in further investments. Cooperation in renewable energy and wind energy technologies has been a core focus of their partnership.

items.title: Geographical branding revolutionized French champagne; are GI tags working for India, too?
items.summary: India has thousands of products unique to a particular area, and the last few years have seen greater impetus to assign them a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, or an geographical origin branding. So far, some stories have played out successfully, while other hold potential to be unlocked.

items.title: Gig workers may get social security benefits through 2% transaction levy on businesses
items.summary: The government is considering implementing a 2% transaction-based levy on aggregators to support social security for gig workers. This levy will fund benefits such as insurance, health, and maternity support for over 12 million workers. There is a consensus that this approach ensures fairness among different types of aggregators. The new scheme is expected to be launched in 2027, requiring gig workers to meet specific work criteria.

items.title: India's palm oil imports hit 14-month high, soyoil purchases set record
items.summary: In October, India experienced a surge in palm oil imports to 866,000 metric tons. Soyoil imports reached a record high of 653,000 tons, reflecting increased demand. The overall edible oil imports rose by 13%, reaching 1.74 million tons during the festive season. This demand is driven by concerns about limited domestic supplies and El Nino-related crop damage.

items.title: US midterm election results impact on Indian economy: From trade deal to oil prices and stock markets, explained
items.summary: While experts expect US President Donald Trump's Republican  party to experience a setback in the US midterm elections, we take a look at what impact these poll results could have on the Indian economy.

items.title: India plans stringent digital locks to secure banking data
items.summary: India is looking to strengthen the digital safeguards protecting sensitive banking information and transactions. The Bureau of Indian Standards plans to update the rules for protecting, storing and transferring encryption keys in line with the latest international norms

items.title: Canva announces major job cuts after 'our hardest year yet'
items.summary: CEO Melanie Perkins says more than 1,000 staff will either lose their jobs or be asked to change roles.

items.title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?
items.summary: Graduates are spending more time managing AI, but are they missing out on other work experience?

items.title: UK and EU agree draft deal to scrap Brexit red tape over food exports
items.summary: The food deal, ahead of a UK-EU summit later this month, is the most significant part of the so-called Brexit reset agreed so far.

items.title: Festive demand lifts dry fruit, chocolate imports this season
items.summary: During the festive season, India's import of tree nuts and chocolates rose significantly, reflecting a 10-12% annual demand increase. The reduction in goods and services tax has made these gourmet products more accessible to consumers. In 2025, dry fruit imports during this period accounted for a substantial share of annual purchases.

items.title: Festive season: Pistachio prices nearly double, almonds up 20% on West Asia crisis and US crop shortfall
items.summary: "Pistachio have been the game spoiler this year. The prices of pistachio from all origins including Iran, Afghanistan and California have increased," said Ravindra Mehta, member of central governing council at Nuts and Dry Fruits Council of India (NDFC-I). "The current pistachio crop in California is expected to be only about 40% of last year, which has led to an increase of 50% in pista prices in the wholesale markets and even more in retail," he added.

items.title: Rs 9,000 crore land assets monetised so far in FY27
items.summary: The NLMC, which is working under the aegis of the Department of Public Enterprises under the finance ministry, also has land assets worth another Rs 4,000-5,000 crore belonging to public sector undertakings (PSUs) in the pipeline. These are at various stages of processing, providing an additional pipeline of potential transactions.
